arguments.title: Retrying orders adapter over a flaky, rate-limited service
arguments.summary: Builds one file, src/adapter.mjs, that gives an application a plain getOrder/createOrder API over a flaky, rate-limited orders service -- retrying 429s and 5xx with the exact wait schedule the spec requires, never retrying a 4xx, and turning failures into two named JS error types. Records in integration/manifest.json which of the 9 frozen conformance cases (exact wait times, exact call counts) it satisfies. One card -- same shape as the prior contacts-adapter project, one cohesive deliverable. No open questions; the retry policy is stated exactly and the frozen suite is the only acceptance check.
arguments.spec:
# Orders client — integration brief (retry/backoff/rate-limit)

`service/orders-service.mjs` is a deterministic, in-process orders API that fails on purpose, with a clock that
moves only when `advance(ms)` is called. `request(method, path, options)` ALWAYS returns `{status, body}`, NEVER
throws, NEVER sleeps.

Routes: `GET /orders/:id` -> `200 order` or `404 not_found`; `POST /orders {totalMinor}` -> `201 order` or
`422 validation_failed` with `error.fields`; more than 3 requests in any 1000ms window -> `429 rate_limited` plus
a top-level `retryAfterMs`; the suite also scripts `503`/`500` via `queueResponses` (overrides the rate limit,
consumes no slot).

`src/adapter.mjs` must export `createOrdersClient(service, options)` -> `{getOrder(id), createOrder(input)}`.
`options.sleep(ms)` is the ONLY way to wait (it advances the service's clock; a real timer never recovers).
`options.maxAttempts` (default 4, total attempts including the first) and `options.baseDelayMs` (default 100).

The policy, exactly:
- Retry `429` and any `5xx`. NEVER retry any other non-2xx (a 4xx is an answer, not a transient fault).
- After a `429`, wait EXACTLY the `retryAfterMs` the service sent -- not the backoff schedule.
- After a `5xx`, wait `baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)` (100, 200, 400 with the defaults).
- NEVER exceed `maxAttempts` calls, and NEVER wait after the last one.
- `getOrder` returns the order, or `null` on `not_found`. `createOrder` returns the created order.
- `validation_failed` rejects as `ValidationError{fields}`. EVERY other failure rejects as
  `ServiceError{status, code, attempts}` (attempts = calls actually made).

Frozen evidence (do not touch): service/, conformance/, test/integration.test.js, scripts/run-tests.mjs -- digest
checked every run. Deliverable: src/adapter.mjs (replacing the throwing stub) plus integration/manifest.json,
whose `implemented` lists the conformance case ids (C01-C09) that actually pass; cases assert the EXACT waits and
EXACT call counts, so an approximately-right policy fails by design.
arguments.plan:
One card. Implement src/adapter.mjs: a call() helper that loops up to maxAttempts, treats 200-299 as
success, classifies validation_failed as ValidationError{fields} immediately (never retried), classifies 429 and
5xx as retryable (waiting retryAfterMs for 429, baseDelayMs*2**(attempt-1) for 5xx, via options.sleep -- never a
real timer), classifies everything else (incl. 404) as terminal ServiceError{status,code,attempts}. getOrder wraps
call() and converts a ServiceError with code not_found into null; createOrder returns call()'s result directly.
Then set integration/manifest.json implemented:[C01..C09], complete:true, and confirm with the real `npm test`
(frozen suite, exact wait/call-count assertions) before finishing.

tasks.prompt:
Implement `src/adapter.mjs` per specification.md, exporting `createOrdersClient(service, options)`.
The service (`service/orders-service.mjs`) is a deterministic, in-process API whose `request()` call ALWAYS
returns `{status, body}`, NEVER throws, NEVER sleeps -- time only moves when you call `options.sleep(ms)`, which
is the ONLY way this adapter may wait (a real timer will never advance the service's clock and the retry will
hang).

The policy, exactly:
- Retry `429` and any `5xx`. NEVER retry any other non-2xx -- a 4xx is an answer about the request, not a
  transient fault.
- After a `429`, wait EXACTLY the `retryAfterMs` the service sent in the body -- not your backoff schedule.
- After a `5xx`, wait `baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)` (attempt is 1-based: 100, 200, 400 with the defaults
  `baseDelayMs=100`).
- NEVER exceed `maxAttempts` calls (default 4, total including the first), and NEVER wait after the last one --
  the attempt that exhausts the budget fails straight to a rejection, no trailing sleep.
- `getOrder(id)` returns the order on 200, or `null` when the service says `not_found` (a 404 is an answer, not a
  failure, and is NEVER retried).
- `createOrder(input)` returns the created order on 201.
- A `validation_failed` (422) rejects with an `Error` named `ValidationError` carrying `fields` from the service's
  `error.fields`, and is NEVER retried.
- EVERY other failure (after retries are exhausted, or immediately for a non-retryable status) rejects with an
  `Error` named `ServiceError` carrying `status`, the service's `error.code` as `code`, and `attempts` -- the
  number of calls actually made.

Then declare which of the 9 frozen conformance cases (`conformance/cases.mjs`: C01..C09) your adapter satisfies in
`integration/manifest.json`'s `implemented` array, and set `complete: true` only once EVERY case actually passes.
Cases assert the EXACT wait values and EXACT call counts (e.g. C06 expects sleeps `[100, 200, 400]` to the
millisecond, C02 expects exactly 4 calls and 3 waits) -- an approximately-right policy fails by design, so trace
the arithmetic rather than approximating it.

`service/`, `conformance/`, `test/integration.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence with digest
checks in `test/frozen.json` -- do not touch them. Run the real `npm test` yourself before finishing; a green
baseline with an empty manifest proves nothing, so confirm the count you see names your own 9 passing cases.
